- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to underreact — forecast is too low; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.7), model overreacts — forecast is too high; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in the 10–15 day horizon; apply a +1.5% bias to forecasts for this window.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3 days, model lags — forecast remains low; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model ignores sentiment volatility — when sentiment swings sharply, forecast remains flat; add 0.3–0.7% adjustment per sentiment swing magnitude.
